reasoning_traces.think:
The core mechanism operates through a two-stage feature decomposition: first, a high-dimensional feature group (B1) captures combinatorial richness up to 8.9 million combinations; second, a lower-dimensional group enables stable parameter estimation. The prior model acts as a regressor of click probability conditioned on these features, effectively modeling historical click behavior. This model is then used to correct implicit relevance signals by discounting or amplifying evidence based on expected click rates—this is the core of presentation bias correction. The multi-model fusion approach ensures that the resulting bias signal is decorrelated from document quality, enhancing robustness. Failure modes arise when feature combinations are too numerous for reliable estimation or when the model fails to distinguish between presentation effects and true relevance.
